_comment: Instrument contract specifications, MEASURED from the broker, never invented.
Every number here was read from MetaTrader5 symbol_info on the account named in `account` below,
at the timestamp in `measured_at`. Nothing in this file is a published figure, a default, or a
reasonable-looking guess: a wrong contract size or tick value sizes every position by the same
wrong factor, and that error is invisible because the arithmetic still looks tidy.
tick_value IS ALREADY IN THE ACCOUNT CURRENCY. This is the single most important line in the file.
The account settles in GBP and both instruments profit in USD, so a conversion is unavoidable - and
the broker has already applied it. XAUUSD: tick_size 0.01 x contract_size 100 = 1.00 USD per tick
per lot, reported as 0.7554981 GBP, which implies USD->GBP 0.7555. BTCUSD: 0.01 x 1 = 0.01 USD per
tick per lot, reported as 0.0075550 GBP - the same rate, which is what makes the two readings
consistent rather than coincidental. So a sizing calculation that uses tick_value needs NO rate of
its own, and must not invent one.
A tick_value is therefore only valid while the exchange rate it embeds is roughly current. It is
stamped with its measurement time so a caller can decide whether it is stale, rather than trusting
a number of unknown age. Refresh with: python -m engine.instrument_specs --refresh
To add an instrument: measure it. Do not copy a row and edit the symbol.

account.note: Vantage demo 11581419, the system's own account. allow_live is false.

XAUUSD.note: 100 troy ounces per lot, so one dollar of price movement is 100 USD on one lot, reported by the broker as 75.54981 GBP.

BTCUSD.note: 1 BTC per lot, which agrees with the holding-cost record in strategy_lab (51.76 USD per 1 BTC per night). min_lot 0.01 means the smallest tradable position is 0.01 BTC.
